summary: myidsan gains a self-service "forgot password" account-recovery flow with two channels. A "Forgot your password?" link on both login surfaces posts to a public, rate-limited, always-generic endpoint (POST /api/login/forgot on the SPA, POST /api/auth/forgot on the server-rendered login page) that never reveals whether the submitted identifier matched an account. Channel 1, always on and air-gap safe: a new superadmin "Reset requests" queue (GET/POST /api/password-reset/*) lets an operator resolve a pending request by issuing a one-time, must-change temporary password to hand over out-of-band, or dismiss a bogus one. Channel 2, optional: a new pure-stdlib infra/mailer SMTP sender (no external dependency) can email a single-use, 30-minute self-service reset link (GET/POST /api/auth/reset) when the new smtp config block is enabled -- the sender refuses to authenticate over a non-STARTTLS connection and strips CR/LF from headers to prevent injection. The self-service link deliberately never issues a session, so any enrolled MFA factor is still presented at the user's next normal login. Only LOCAL accounts are eligible; LDAP/Kerberos/OIDC accounts are silently excluded and directed to their upstream identity provider. Live-benched end-to-end: no-oracle response, SMTP self-service reset, admin-queue resolve to temp-password to must-change, single-use token consumption, and dismiss.
compatibility: Purely additive and opt-in. One new DB table (password_reset_request, auto-added by bootstrap schema generation); no changes to any existing table or endpoint default. The new smtp config block defaults fully disabled (absent from config.json/config.dev.json decodes to the Go zero value) -- an existing or air-gapped install is completely unaffected until an operator explicitly sets smtp.enabled=true and points it at an internal relay; the operator reset queue works with zero configuration either way. No config migration needed.
